record.original_question: Fix r >= 2. How large can lambda_1(G) + lambda_n(G) be among all K_{r+1}-free graphs G of order n?

evidence.quote: Problem 9 (Brandt [27]). Let r ≥ 2. How large can λ_1(G) + λ_n(G) be if G is a K_{r+1}-free graph of order n ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $A(G)$ be its adjacency matrix with real eigenvalues $\lambda_1(G) \ge \lambda_2(G) \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n(G)$. For an integer $r \ge 2$, call $G$ a $K_{r+1}$-free graph if $G$ contains no clique on $r+1$ vertices.

Determine, as a function of $n$ and $r$, the maximum possible value of
$$\lambda_1(G) + \lambda_n(G)$$
taken over all $K_{r+1}$-free graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices, and characterize the extremal graphs attaining this maximum.
artifact.status_search_result: For the case r = 2 (triangle-free graphs), Brandt's conjecture on the sum of the largest and smallest adjacency eigenvalues has been studied extensively, with bounds (originally for regular graphs, later extended) proved in recent works such as "The Spectrum of Triangle-Free Graphs" (SIDMA, 2023) and a related note by Csikvári. The general problem for arbitrary r ≥ 2 (sharp maximum of λ_1 + λ_n among K_{r+1}-free graphs of order n) does not appear to have a complete published solution; it remains open in general, with only partial results in low-r and regular-graph cases.

status_evidence.title: The Spectrum of Triangle-Free Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies sum of largest and smallest adjacency eigenvalues for triangle-free graphs, addressing Brandt-type problem for r=2.
status_evidence.claim: The r=2 case has been substantially advanced with new bounds on λ_1 + λ_n for triangle-free graphs.

status_evidence.title: Note on the sum of the smallest and largest eigenvalues of a triangle-free graph
status_evidence.snippet: Provides bounds on λ_1(G)+λ_n(G) for triangle-free graphs G.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists on the r=2 instance of Brandt's problem.
